page: Microsoft Azure F48ams_v6 is a high-capacity virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture, featuring a dedicated 48-core AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. Configured with a 1:1 mapping of 48 physical cores to 48 vCPUs (one thread per core), the instance avoids hyper-threading contention. It provides 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Hardware acceleration flags include AVX-512 extensions (F, VNNI, and BF16) alongside SHA-NI and AES cryptographic instructions. The instance does not include local disk storage or hardware GPUs, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage.

Benchmark data reflects exceptional parallel throughput. Multi-core compute performance sits in the top 10% across stress-ng, Geekbench 6 multi-core, Clang compilation, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression tests. Memory throughput demonstrates strong capability, reaching 226.16 GB/sec in uncached 256 MB read operations and 144.16 GB/sec write bandwidth. Small-model LLM prompt processing (135M parameters) places in the top tier at 5369.82 tokens per second, aided by AVX-512 BF16 support. Single-threaded tasks, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, perform in the middle 50% tier, showing that the architecture delivers its primary advantage in horizontally distributed execution.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the F48ams_v6 delivers high resource efficiency for setups requiring simultaneous multi-core compute density and elevated memory allocations per core. The absence of local scratch disks requires external block storage planning, which trades bundled storage convenience for flexible capacity scaling. The server fits database engines, high-concurrency Redis caching, parallel software build systems, and batch CPU-bound data pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure F48ams_v6 is a compute and memory-intensive virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor at 3.7 GHz, delivering 48 dedicated physical cores with single-thread-per-core mapping. It features 384.0 GB of RAM, offering a substantial 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation alongside AVX-512 vector instruction support. The instance operates without local storage or discrete GPUs, requiring external storage integration. In performance testing, the instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core metrics, including Geekbench multi-core, software compilation under Clang, and multi-threaded decompression. Memory throughput remains robust, supporting large-block transfers at over 226 GB/sec read speeds. Single-core throughput places in the average to strong categories, confirming that system efficiency peaks during heavily parallelized execution. This hardware profile suits memory-heavy databases, high-throughput Redis deployments, large-scale CI/CD build environments, and parallel analytical workloads.
